definition.equivalent: no input makes the mutated engine observably different; an argument from the code, not a proof
definition.verdict: some input changes a certification, an obligation, a decision or the released C; direction says how (unsound-possible: something is certified, admitted or released that the unmutated engine refuses or that differs from the source's meaning; conservative; crash; other)
definition.report: only a message, an identity, text layout of the released C, an ordering or a resource limit changes
definition.defensive: the changed code is not reached through the public entry points, as far as was argued

mutants.reason: `active[-0]` is active[0]: an #else inside a nested conditional flips the outermost entry instead of the innermost. The shipped headers nest conditionals too, but there the two readings coincide (verified by reading pfc.h: the inner #else has both entries true and nothing follows the inner #endif). In user code a nested #ifdef/#else changes which lines are read, so a function can be skipped (not checked, not released) or a branch a C compiler ignores can be read. Unsound with respect to the source file: the mutant certifies a file whose contract is false under C's own lexical rules; the released C matches what the mutant read, so the release is self-consistent.

mutants.reason: admitted(): an unproved root is no longer recorded as False in `known`. `known` is read through known.get (None is as falsy as False) and `dependency in known`; for an unproved dependency the same condition list ends in `dependency not in proved`, which gives the same False verdict, and the result keeps only True entries. Probed: 40 000 random dependency graphs (cycles, missing dependencies, unproved nodes, shuffled order) give the same frozenset as the original admitted().

mutants.reason: admitted(): the nodes of a failed path are no longer recorded as False. Their iterators stay in `pending` (it is only deleted on success), so any later dependency on them is rejected by `dependency in pending`, and when one is itself visited as a root its first non-admitted dependency is again unproved, missing, or still in `pending`; it can never become True. Only repeated work differs. Probed: 40 000 random dependency graphs (cycles, missing dependencies, unproved nodes, shuffled order) give the same frozenset as the original admitted().

mutants.reason: _range is the type-domain of every bool (parameters, globals, array reads, loop-havocked variables, call results) and also the result-domain guarantee of ExternalCheck (wp.external). With -1..1 the hypotheses get weaker (conservative), but the external-contract satisfiability check gets weaker too, so an impossible contract of a declared-only bool function is accepted and then assumed by callers (rule 6 broken).
mutants.witness: work/vc/p4.c: `bool odd(long x) ensures(result + 1 == 0); long use(long x) { long k = odd(x); return k; }` -> original: not certified (contract of odd cannot be satisfied); mutant: certified (full), 'declared functions trusted: 1'. Conservative side: work/vc/p2.c: `long idx(long n, long a[n], bool b) requires(n == 2) { long x = b; return a[x]; }` -> original certified, mutant not certified (counterexample b = -1).
mutants.test_idea: A declared-only bool function with ensures(result == -1) must be refused as contradictory; and a bool parameter used as index into a 2-element array must certify.

mutants.reason: With low = 1 every type-domain hypothesis for a bool becomes b == 1, so the checker assumes every bool parameter/global/array element/call result is true; any path under !b is treated as dead and its bounds/division checks are proved and removed. Entry consistency stays sat, so nothing else catches it.
mutants.witness: work/vc/p1.c: `long pick(long n, long a[n], bool b) requires(n == 2) { if (!b) { return a[5]; } return a[0]; }` -> original: not certified (a[5] may be outside, counterexample n = 2, b = 0); mutant: certified (full), bounds checks removed 2 of 2, i.e. the guard of an out-of-bounds read reachable with b = false is deleted.
mutants.test_idea: A function reading out of bounds only when a bool parameter is false must be refused with a counterexample where the bool is 0.

mutants.reason: Same site as vc-0016, upper bound 2 instead of 1: bool type-domain hypotheses weaken (conservative), but the result-domain guarantee of the external-contract check weakens as well, so a declared-only bool function promising result == 2 is accepted and callers assume it (dead-path reasoning over a value a C _Bool never has).

mutants.reason: _measure's size feeds Generator.named (threshold MEMORY_NAMING = 200) and the cumulative term_count limit in Generator.add. Counting 2 per node makes write chains get a fresh named memory with an extra 'allocation' same-memory hypothesis about twice as early, so obligations, their identities and the solver queries differ, and the 5,000,000-node vc-complexity limit is reached at half the size.
